reasoning: Failure-driven edits take priority and are all kept: the answer line, the archive-page cue, the expanded DELETE-CLUE-WORDS replace (with the now-redundant 'one of these / Balloon' bullet deleted so Rule 4 shrinks), the plural/number replace, and the SLOT HEAD PHRASE bullet with its substitution test. Both groups proposed a mandatory three-field answer line at the top of the editable part. I merged them into the failure version (support 2) and added one clause saying it is the single check line, so it does not clash with the protected block's check line. From the success group I kept three bullets that fill gaps the failure edits leave: (1) the cut-off or clue-only snippet bullet (support 2), shortened to avoid stacking on the archive-page cue; (2) bare definition/etymology clues; (3) a full quoted line asks for its author. The last two both targeted the same anchor, so I combined them into one insert to avoid an ordering conflict. They agree with the optimizer memory's guidance on quote clues. I dropped the success group's duplicate answer-line edit. No edit touches the SLOW_UPDATE block, and Rule 3's verbatim-archive override is left intact.

edits.content:
## MANDATORY ANSWER LINE (write it before every answer)
Write exactly one short line before the answer tags: `Type: <noun the clue asks for> | Evidence: <quoted passage line, or own fact> | Check: <candidate put into the clue's blank reads correctly, is that type, and is not a word already in the clue>`. If Check fails, change the candidate. This is the single check line for every answer, so do not write a second one. The detailed rules below explain how to fill each field. Then put only the bare answer in the tags.

edits.target: ## Rule 3: Look for the clue repeated verbatim in the context
edits.content: - ARCHIVE-PAGE CUE: passages titled like 'jeopardy/NNNN_Qs.txt ... GitHub', 'J! Archive', 'jService' or flashcard pages hold the clue followed by '| answer. right: Name.'. Scan them FIRST and match on a distinctive fragment of the clue (a rare word, a place, the first few words), even if the clue opens with a parenthetical like '(Sarah of the Clue Crew ...)'. Copy the text between '|' and '. right:' and do not replace it with your own guess, even when most other passages are junk. Never copy stray glued characters from scraped text ('ragaE'); give the clean word.

edits.target: - DELETE-CLUE-WORDS TEST: before answering, strike from your candidate every specific word or phrase the clue already states, and keep only the remaining head. 'Bret Harte wrote about these exiles "of Poker Flat"' -> 'The Outcasts' (not 'The Outcasts of Poker Flat'). 'Robert La Follette called it the Progressive party, but it was nicknamed this' -> 'Bull Moose' (not 'Bull Moose Party'). 'This funeral structure' -> 'Pyre' (not 'funeral pyre', and not 'funeral boat', which echoes the clue's 'funeral' and ignores that the passages say 'funeral pyre').
edits.content: - DELETE-CLUE-WORDS TEST: before answering, strike from your candidate (a) every word or phrase the clue already states, including ordinals and adjectives ('the third leader ... to bear this title' -> 'Dalai Lama', not 'third Dalai Lama'); (b) a type noun the clue already supplies ('this party', 'these mountains', 'this company') when the short name stands alone; (c) modifiers copied from passages when the clue says only 'this / one of these <generic noun>' ('hot air', 'funeral', 'synthetic'), unless they are part of the standard proper name. Keep the remaining head. 'Bret Harte wrote about these exiles "of Poker Flat"' -> 'The Outcasts' (not 'The Outcasts of Poker Flat'). 'Robert La Follette called it the Progressive party, but it was nicknamed this' -> 'Bull Moose' (not 'Bull Moose Party'). 'This funeral structure' -> 'Pyre' (not 'funeral pyre' or 'funeral boat'). 'a back shaped like one of these' -> 'Balloon' (not 'hot air balloon'). Clue-supplied ordinals, adjectives and suffixes are never covered by the head-noun exception below.

edits.target: - When the clue says only 'one of these' / 'this <generic noun>' and the answer is a common noun, give the plain common noun with no added modifiers: 'a back shaped like one of these' -> 'Balloon' (not 'hot air balloon'). Modifiers copied from passages (hot air, synthetic, funeral, speech) are usually wrong unless part of the standard proper name.
- Use the singular form for a generic single object ('Well', not 'wells'), but keep the plural for crops, commodities and mass categories ('Bananas') or when the clue says 'these'/'ones'.
edits.content: - Match the grammatical number of the clue's noun phrase. Use the singular for a generic single object ('Well', not 'wells'), but keep the plural for crops, commodities and mass categories ('Bananas'), when the clue says 'these'/'ones', or when the clue's noun is plural. A 'this fruit / vegetable / grain / crop' clue in a festival, harvest or market context names the crop as a mass category, so answer plural ('Strawberries').

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content:
- SLOT HEAD PHRASE: the noun phrase around 'this' (or the pronoun) names the CATEGORY you must answer in. Passages are full of related words from other categories, and those are wrong. Name the category first, then run the SUBSTITUTION TEST: put the candidate into the clue's blank. If the result is the wrong kind of thing, or repeats a noun already in the clue, reject it. The head-noun exception in Rule 4 applies only when the clue's own 'this <type>' IS the head of the named entity ('this purchase' -> Gadsden Purchase), not when the clue's noun is a different category (city, acid, person).
  - 'this part of the <plant / body / machine>' -> a PART noun (roots, valve), not the process or function the passages explain (absorption, circulation).
  - 'this type / kind / variety of <noun>' -> a named kind that forms a compound with that noun, never a bare material or adjective ('natural', 'synthetic').
  - 'the energy / light / heat from this', 'X is measured by a <instrument>' -> the SOURCE or object itself, not the quantity measured or a descriptive phrase.
  - 'Her / His <home, house, studio, birthplace>' that is now a museum or landmark -> the PERSON. Do not add 'Museum', 'House' or 'Birthplace'.

edits.target: Do not talk yourself out of a well-supported entity.
edits.content: - Cut-off or clue-only snippets (an archive page shows the clue with no answer, or passages are dominated by an anchor such as a well, a battle or a cast): never abstain and never answer with the anchor or a clue word. Re-read the clue's category noun and its numbers or dates, then name the entity of that category that sibling passages tie to those details, confirmed by your own knowledge. Give the plain term the passages repeat, with no added descriptors, in the plural if the clue says 'these'.

edits.target: - 'N-word' hints ('this 3-word phrase') work like a letter count: the answer must have exactly N words.
edits.content:
- BARE DEFINITION / ETYMOLOGY clues with no 'this' and no 'Term for' ('A short, witty saying'; 'From the Middle Dutch for "little barrel", it's another word for yokel'): the answer is the single word being defined. Find the dictionary, thesaurus or crossword passage whose headword is glossed with the clue's own words, and answer with that headword as a plain word, not a longer phrase, an example of the thing, or a synonym that fits only part of the clue.
- A FULL QUOTED LINE (verse, lyric, speech) with no '...' blank and no 'this <work>' asks for its AUTHOR or SPEAKER. Passages pair the line with headings like 'Poem by X' or '<Title> by X'. Answer the person's name (usually the famous surname form the passages use), not the work's title or a word from the line. If the clue has '...' or says 'this poem/song', the slot is the missing words or the title instead.
